hero.title: The Four Noble Truths: Buddhism
hero.description: The foundational philosophical framework of Buddhism as expounded by Siddhartha Gautama in the Dhamma-cakka-ppavattana Sutta.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Tenets

  • Dukkha: Universal suffering
  • Samudaya: Tanha (Trishna)
  • Nirodha: Cessation of desire
  • Magga: Ashtangika Marga

Context

  • Sermon: Sarnath
  • Audience: Five Ascetics
  • Scripture: Sutta Pitaka
  • The 4 Arya Satyani:
    • 1. Dukkha: The world is full of misery. Birth, death, and old age are painful.
    • 2. Samudaya: The cause is Trishna (craving/attachment).
    • 3. Nirodha: Removing Trishna achieves Nirvana.
    • 4. Magga: The path to liberation is the Middle Path (Madhyama Pratipada).

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Tracing the birth and formalization of the core Buddhist tenets.

cards.details: Siddhartha Gautama attains Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and delivers his first sermon at Sarnath (Dhamma-cakka-ppavattana).
Immediately after the Mahaparinibbana of Buddha at Rajgir; compilation of Sutta Pitaka begins.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Memory triggers for the four truths.

items.title: D.C.N.E
items.decryption: D (Dukkha - Suffering exists), C (Cause/Samudaya - Desire is the cause), N (Nirodha - Suffering can be ended), E (Eightfold path - The solution).

items: Thinking the Four Noble Truths imply that life is 'evil'. Buddhism emphasizes life as 'dukkha' (unsatisfactory/transient), not morally evil.
Confusing 'Samudaya' (Origin) with 'Nirodha' (Cessation). Remember: Samudaya is the 'why', Nirodha is the 'how to stop'.
